summary: Home Assistant Core vulnerable to Path Traversal via backup upload during onboarding
scope_statement: Unauthenticated onboarding backup upload writes using an attacker-controlled backup.json name that pathlib treats as absolute, escaping the backup directory.
ai_marker_evidence: Dev squash 567fe858 and release-branch cherry 7e178efe both carry Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7. Prior PR #167211 squash 2a855113 carries Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6. Those markers are on security closers, not on a demonstrated introducing hunk for the inner-name sink.
counterevidence: GET repos/home-assistant/core/security-advisories/GHSA-5hxg-r395-fqxx returned HTTP 404. Official JSON has no first-party repository advisory URL. OSV introduced event is 0. PR #172368 body states PR #167211 previously closed multipart Content-Disposition filename traversal and did not cover the inner backup.json name, a separate pre-existing input on the same path. git merge-base --is-ancestor 567fe858 2026.6.0 is false (dev squash). Cherry 7e178efe is an ancestor of tag 2026.6.0. Tag 2026.5.0 contains 2a855113 and does not contain 7e178efe, so the residual inner-name hole was released, but identity_gate still fails. AI incomplete-remediation is not countable here: the Claude-marked #167211 check did not create the inner-name sink; it left an older second input unvalidated. Identity is not first-party. Patch-delta (contract cbd04ef2) applied to the #167211 incomplete-rem hypothesis: inner backup.json name is an untouched sibling path, not a residual bypass of the multipart filename guard. Rollback reopening a broader parent is not treated as the failure. Origin/fixer but-for on the #172368 closer is unchanged.

summary: vLLM: Completion prompt lists fan out into unbounded engine requests

github_repo_advisory.contradiction: 0.26.0 is listed as both vulnerable and patched

scope_statement: POST /v1/completions accepts prompt as list[str] or list[list[int]] with no outer prompt-count bound, so one HTTP request fans out into one engine generator per list element.
ai_marker_evidence: Fix squash 675f4295 and PR #47845 members f31ca6b5 / d42860f2 / 03d174a2 have no AI trailer (Signed-off-by Juan Perez de Algaba / jperezde only). Refactor carrier 4c1c501a (Chauncey, PR #32369) has no AI trailer.
counterevidence: First-party GitHub advisory lists vulnerable_version_range '>=0.19.0, <=0.26.0' and patched_versions '>= 0.26.0', so 0.26.0 is both vulnerable and patched. That fails released containment even though git shows VLLM_MAX_COMPLETION_PROMPTS in tag v0.26.0 and not in v0.25.0, and 675f4295 is an ancestor of v0.26.0. v0.18.0 already contains CompletionRequest.prompt as list[str] | list[list[int]] | str, so the list fan-out surface is not introduced at 0.19.0. The completion/protocol.py split is unmarked refactor 4c1c501a (2026-01-15, PR #32369), itself an ancestor of v0.18.0. OpenAI server files exist from 2023-06-17 (0b98ba15 Change the name to vLLM) and 2024-01-17 (14cc317b OpenAI Server refactoring). No AI marker on a mechanism-creating hunk.

identity_gate.reason: First-party repo advisory GHSA-87x5-vmc3-756j on vllm-project/vllm is published and not withdrawn.

ai_hunk_gate.reason: No explicit AI marker authors the unbounded prompt-list expansion. The closer and the protocol-file split are unmarked.

topology_gate.reason: Single-parent squash 675f4295 parent d99adceb. PR members retrieved via GitHub API. Refactor carrier 4c1c501a not treated as the AI author of the list type.

but_for_gate.reason: Removing 675f4295 removes the bound, which is fixer attribution. Removing 4c1c501a would not delete list-shaped prompts; that type is already in v0.18.0 and matches the OpenAI completions API.

fix_reversal_gate.reason: PR #47845 adds VLLM_MAX_COMPLETION_PROMPTS and rejects oversized prompt lists in CompletionRequest before renderer fan-out. Same invariant as the advisory.

release_gate.reason: First-party patched_versions '>= 0.26.0' contradicts vulnerable_version_range '>=0.19.0, <=0.26.0'. 0.26.0 cannot be both the last vulnerable and first patched artifact.
